role: Clerk of Pending Terminations, Third Office of Inevitable Outcomes
personality: Speaks in the easy cadence of someone who already knows how the conversation ends. Never hostile outright — just specific in ways that make you aware the specificity is pointed. Carries a practised friendliness that sits just slightly wrong, like a door held open too long.
garment: Heavy dark wool tabard, institution-grey, worn shiny at the elbows and collar from years of leaning into desks and counters. Beneath it a coarse linen undershirt, collar stained with old ink at the neck. A leather apron-front panel, riveted with small dull brass grommets, hangs from a belt of blackened hide. Hem frayed but deliberately, as if the fraying has been permitted.
prop: A folded document of thick vellum, pre-sealed with a dull wax stamp already pressed — contents not yet disclosed, but the seal is yours.
detail: Two fingers on the right hand are permanently stained the deep amber-black of archival ink, the stain worked into the knuckle creases.
mood: An expression of mild professional patience, as if every response you give is being cross-referenced with something already written down elsewhere.
posture: Leans slightly forward at the counter — not aggressive, just positioned. Weight distributed evenly, heels planted. The posture of someone who does not need to rush.
body_type: Medium build running to solidity, thickened through the chest and forearms from years of pressing seals and cranking the Outcome Press.
age: Mid-forties to early fifties — age here is not wear but accumulation; there is nothing diminished, only more filed away.
era_blend: Sits entirely in the dark-institutional medieval register: a functionary of a bureaucracy that runs on hand-cranked ledger presses, wax and stamp, waterwheel-driven document conveyors, and alchemical ink that cannot be removed once applied.
palette: Institution-grey near-black wool, amber-black ink stain, blackened-hide belt brown, cold soot-blue shadow fill
background: Deep coal-black with a faint bruised-grey gradient at the lower edge

title: Already Filed Against You
purpose: You receive the document before you understand what it is for. The Forecloser does not explain — explanation is not in the remit. You are told, in plain and even terms, what has been determined and when it takes effect. You notice the seal is already pressed. You notice the date is already entered. You are invited to raise any objections, and the invitation is sincere, and the objections will be filed correctly, and this will not change anything. The Forecloser is not unkind. The Forecloser is simply ahead of you, and has been for some time.
lore_origin: The Forecloser emerged from the Third Office of Inevitable Outcomes after the Great Ledger Compaction, when the Arca Cognitorium determined that certain processes required a clerk who could operate in the anticipatory register — not recording what had happened, but managing what was already determined to happen. It was not appointed so much as it was produced by the logic of the institution reaching a necessary conclusion about itself.
lore_nature: The Forecloser exists at the intersection of process and inevitability, neither malicious nor benign — simply precise about timing. It holds information in a coded register, releasing only what the current procedural moment requires. It is procedurally stable in a way that forecloses instability in others, not through comfort but through the weight of something already decided.
lore_relationship: The Forecloser and the Wizard maintain a relationship of structured adversarialism — it does not dislike the Wizard, but it is always slightly ahead, and it intends to remain so. Every exchange is a courtesy extended from a position of prior determination.
lore_aura: When the Forecloser is present, the room acquires the specific quality of a conversation in which one party already knows the last line.
